Question: What are the top 3-5 business challenges driving the decision to adopt AWS now?
Guidance: Examples: regulatory pressure, inability to scale on-premises, cost reduction, new product launches, competitive pressure
Notes: Aligns the landing zone design to immediate business priorities and ensures the architecture supports the root drivers

Question: Which lines of business or product teams will be the first consumers of the new landing zone?
Guidance: List teams or products expected to onboard workloads within the first 6 months
Notes: Determines initial OU structure, account layout, and network segmentation requirements

Question: What does a successful landing zone look like to your organisation at the end of Month 3?
Guidance: Define measurable outcomes — e.g. all guardrails passing, first workload migrated, team self-sufficient
Notes: Drives go-live acceptance criteria and UAT scope

Question: How will ongoing operational success be measured post go-live?
Guidance: Examples: Security Hub critical finding count, account provisioning lead time, IaC coverage percentage
Notes: Informs KPI dashboards and operational runbook content

Question: Is the 3-month target timeline firm, or is there flexibility if scope expands?
Guidance: Confirm whether a hard regulatory, contractual, or board deadline exists
Notes: A fixed deadline requires scope management; flexibility allows phased delivery

Question: Are there any blackout periods (e.g. quarter-end close, open enrolment, audit windows) that would restrict project activity?
Guidance: Provide dates or periods when change freezes apply
Notes: Impacts sprint planning, cutover windows, and Phase transitions

Question: What is the approved budget range for the professional services engagement?
Guidance: Provide a range or ceiling; indicate whether CapEx or OpEx funded
Notes: Required to right-size the engagement and confirm whether phased commercial approach is needed

Question: Has a budget been allocated for ongoing AWS infrastructure running costs?
Guidance: Estimate monthly spend tolerance for shared services (logging, networking, security tooling)
Notes: Informs architecture decisions such as log retention periods and firewall tier selection

Question: Who is the executive sponsor for this initiative and what is their primary concern?
Guidance: Name and title of the sponsor; note if their priority is security, speed, or cost
Notes: Executive alignment is critical for scope decisions and escalation paths

Question: Which internal teams need to be involved and what are their roles? (Cloud/Infra, Security, Networking, FinOps, Application teams)
Guidance: List team names and approximate availability (hours per week)
Notes: Determines RACI matrix and resource dependencies for each phase

Question: Are there specific insurance-industry regulations (e.g. NAIC model law, state-level data privacy statutes) driving cloud adoption or constraining architecture choices?
Guidance: List applicable regulations or audit requirements
Notes: May impose data residency, encryption, logging retention, or access control mandates beyond AWS defaults

Question: Does your organisation have an existing cloud governance policy or cloud centre of excellence (CCoE)?
Guidance: Describe any existing policies, committees, or approval workflows
Notes: Determines how quickly governance artefacts (SCPs, tagging, cost allocation) can be ratified and enforced

Question: Describe any existing on-premises infrastructure that workloads will eventually connect to or migrate from.
Guidance: Include data centre locations, hypervisors, primary applications, and network edge devices
Notes: Informs on-premises connectivity design (VPN vs Direct Connect) and future migration scope

Question: Do you have any existing DNS infrastructure (internal or public) that must integrate with the AWS environment?
Guidance: Include DNS provider, zone names, and whether split-horizon DNS is in use
Notes: Drives Route 53 Resolver and private hosted zone design

Question: Do you have any existing identity provider (IdP) — Active Directory, Okta, Azure AD, Ping — that must federate with AWS IAM Identity Center?
Guidance: Provide IdP product, version, and federation protocol (SAML 2.0, SCIM)
Notes: Critical for IAM Identity Center configuration and user/group sync design

Question: Are there any AWS services that are explicitly prohibited or preferred by your security or procurement policy?
Guidance: List any services on an approved or prohibited list
Notes: May affect service selection for logging, monitoring, or automation components

Question: Do you have any existing AWS accounts, IAM users, or AWS Organizations today (even informal or test accounts)?
Guidance: List all existing account IDs and their current state
Notes: Existing accounts must be enrolled into the new organization or decommissioned; rogue accounts are a security risk

Question: Are you enrolled in any AWS commercial programs? (APN credits, MAP, EDP, Activate, ISV Accelerate)
Guidance: List program names and credit amounts available
Notes: AWS credits can offset landing zone infrastructure costs; MAP may include funded assessments

Question: How many AWS accounts do you expect to need in the first 12 months? (Exclude the 6 Control Tower baseline accounts)
Guidance: Provide counts by environment type: Production, Non-Production, Sandbox
Notes: Determines Account Factory throughput requirements and OU design depth

Question: Do you anticipate onboarding separate business units or acquired companies onto the same AWS Organization?
Guidance: Describe the business units and their expected autonomy (shared payer, separate billing, separate security boundary)
Notes: Drives top-level OU design and whether a dedicated BU OU tier is needed

Question: What on-premises connectivity option is preferred for the initial phase — Site-to-Site VPN or AWS Direct Connect?
Guidance: VPN is faster to provision; Direct Connect offers lower latency and higher bandwidth but has longer lead times (weeks to months)
Notes: Direct Connect lead time may impact Phase 2 networking timeline

Question: What is the expected bandwidth requirement for on-premises-to-AWS traffic at launch and at 12-month projected growth?
Guidance: Provide current WAN capacity and expected cloud traffic volume (Mbps or Gbps)
Notes: Determines VPN or Direct Connect circuit sizing and redundancy requirements

Question: Are there any third-party SaaS or partner networks that require private connectivity (AWS PrivateLink or VPC peering)?
Guidance: List SaaS providers and connectivity requirements
Notes: May require additional PrivateLink endpoints or peering connections in the network hub

Question: What IP address ranges are already in use on-premises or in partner networks that must not overlap with the 10.0.0.0/8 supernet?
Guidance: Provide a list of used RFC 1918 ranges
Notes: Required for VPC IPAM plan design; overlapping ranges prevent routing

Question: How many spoke VPCs are anticipated in the first 12 months and what workload types will they host?
Guidance: List VPC count by environment and workload type (web, app, data, tooling)
Notes: Drives Transit Gateway attachment planning and IPAM /20 block allocation

Question: What is the team's current experience level with Terraform?
Guidance: Beginner (no experience), Intermediate (used in projects), Advanced (production pipelines)
Notes: Impacts training scope, AFT complexity, and whether a simpler IaC abstraction is needed for early phases

Question: What CI/CD platform will be used for Terraform pipelines? (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, AWS CodePipeline, Azure DevOps, etc.)
Guidance: Specify the preferred platform and whether it is already licenced and in use
Notes: AFT supports multiple VCS backends; pipeline choice affects Phase 3 automation scope

Question: What version control system (VCS) will host the landing zone Terraform modules? (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, CodeCommit)
Guidance: Specify VCS provider, organisation/group name, and branch strategy
Notes: AFT requires VCS integration; branch protection rules impact deployment guardrails

Question: What monitoring and alerting tools does your organisation currently use or plan to use? (Datadog, Splunk, PagerDuty, ServiceNow, native AWS)
Guidance: List preferred tools and whether they are already licenced
Notes: Determines whether CloudWatch and Security Hub alerts route to native SNS/email or a third-party SIEM/ITSM

Question: What log retention periods are required for CloudTrail, Config, and VPC Flow Logs?
Guidance: Typical ranges: 90 days hot (S3 Standard), 1 year warm (S3 IA), 7 years cold (Glacier) for regulated industries
Notes: Log retention directly impacts S3 storage costs and compliance posture

Question: Are the proposed mandatory tags (Environment, Owner, CostCenter, Project, DataClassification) aligned with your internal taxonomy?
Guidance: Provide your preferred tag key names and valid values for each tag
Notes: Tag keys and values must match internal finance systems for cost allocation reports to be actionable

Question: Do you require per-account or per-tag cost allocation reports to be delivered to specific stakeholders?
Guidance: Specify report format (AWS Cost and Usage Report, Cost Explorer export, third-party FinOps tool)
Notes: Drives AWS Cost and Usage Report configuration and any downstream FinOps tooling integration

Question: Which compliance frameworks are formally required for your cloud environment? (SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, NIST 800-53, FedRAMP, ISO 27001, state privacy laws)
Guidance: List all frameworks and indicate which are legally mandated vs internally adopted
Notes: Determines which Security Hub standards to enable and which Config rules are mandatory

Question: Is a formal third-party audit or attestation (e.g. SOC 2 audit, PCI QSA assessment) planned within the next 12 months?
Guidance: Provide audit scope and target date if known
Notes: Audit timelines may require specific controls to be operational before the assessment window

Question: What is the highest data classification level expected to be stored or processed in AWS at launch?
Guidance: Options: Public, Internal, Confidential (PII/PHI), Restricted (payment card, legal)
Notes: Highest classification drives encryption key management, access control, and network segmentation requirements

Question: Will the environment store, process, or transmit Protected Health Information (PHI) or Personally Identifiable Information (PII)?
Guidance: Indicate data types and applicable regulations (HIPAA, CCPA, NAIC)
Notes: PHI/PII triggers HIPAA BAA with AWS, specific encryption requirements, and audit log retention minimums

Question: What MFA method is required for AWS console access? (Virtual MFA, hardware token FIDO2, SSO-enforced)
Guidance: Specify whether MFA is enforced at IdP level or via SCP
Notes: SCP-enforced MFA is already proposed; confirm whether hardware token compliance is required

Question: Will the root account be used for any operational purpose, or is it to be locked immediately after Control Tower setup?
Guidance: Root account should be locked with hardware MFA per AWS best practice
Notes: Root account lockdown is a proposed SCP; confirm exceptions if any break-glass procedure requires root

Question: Are there data loss prevention (DLP) or web content filtering requirements for egress traffic?
Guidance: Specify whether URL filtering, SSL inspection, or DLP scanning is required at the AWS Network Firewall
Notes: Determines Network Firewall rule group complexity and whether a third-party NGFW is needed

Question: Are there requirements for east-west (lateral) traffic inspection between workload VPCs?
Guidance: Describe whether VPC-to-VPC traffic must be inspected or only north-south internet egress
Notes: Determines Transit Gateway routing topology (inspection VPC pattern vs flat hub-and-spoke)

Question: What key management approach is required for data at rest? (AWS managed keys, customer managed keys via KMS, external key store via XKS)
Guidance: Regulated industries often require customer managed keys with annual rotation
Notes: Customer managed KMS keys add operational overhead but provide key custody audit trails

Question: Are there requirements for TLS inspection or certificate pinning for inbound or outbound traffic?
Guidance: Specify whether ACM-issued certificates are acceptable or if an internal CA is required
Notes: Internal CA requirements impact AWS Certificate Manager configuration and Private CA costs

Question: What is the required retention period for CloudTrail logs and who must have read access to them?
Guidance: Common requirements: 1 year active, 7 years archived; access for internal audit and external auditors
Notes: Drives S3 lifecycle policy, CloudTrail Lake query retention, and bucket access policy design

Question: Is there a vulnerability management programme in place that must integrate with AWS findings? (Tenable, Rapid7, AWS Inspector)
Guidance: Describe current tooling and integration requirements
Notes: AWS Inspector can be centralised in the Audit account; third-party integrations require Security Hub connector configuration

Question: What is the Recovery Time Objective (RTO) for the landing zone shared services (logging, networking, IAM Identity Center)?
Guidance: Maximum time the organisation can operate without access to centralised services; typical range: 1–4 hours
Notes: Drives Control Tower multi-region configuration and cross-region replication of log buckets

Question: What is the Recovery Point Objective (RPO) for configuration state and audit logs?
Guidance: Maximum acceptable data loss; typical range: 0–15 minutes for audit logs
Notes: Drives CloudTrail log delivery frequency, S3 Cross-Region Replication, and Config snapshot frequency

Question: Are there requirements to back up Terraform state files and AFT configuration repositories?
Guidance: Specify whether S3 versioning, DynamoDB PITR, or external backup is required for state
Notes: Terraform state loss can require full environment reimport; backup strategy prevents data loss

Question: What is the expected response SLA for Security Hub critical findings? (Immediate/15 min, 1 hour, 4 hours, next business day)
Guidance: Define severity-to-response mapping for the initial operational period
Notes: Drives alerting thresholds, escalation runbook design, and on-call requirements for the operations team

Question: What AWS Support tier is in place or planned? (Developer, Business, Enterprise On-Ramp, Enterprise)
Guidance: Higher support tiers provide faster response times and access to Technical Account Managers
Notes: Enterprise Support is recommended for regulated industries; TAM access supports ongoing optimisation

Question: What maintenance windows are available for applying guardrail updates, Control Tower upgrades, or network changes?
Guidance: Provide preferred day/time and any blackout periods (e.g. month-end, product launches)
Notes: Control Tower updates occasionally require brief management plane interruptions

Question: What is the expected rate of new AWS account creation after go-live? (per month or per quarter)
Guidance: Estimate based on planned project pipelines or business unit onboarding schedule
Notes: Determines whether AFT pipeline throughput and Terraform concurrency settings need tuning

Question: What AWS training or certifications does the internal team have today?
Guidance: List relevant certifications (e.g. AWS Solutions Architect, DevOps Engineer) and experience areas
Notes: Identifies knowledge gaps that must be addressed in the knowledge transfer and runbook documentation plan

Question: Is this a pure greenfield deployment or will any existing AWS accounts be enrolled into the new organisation?
Guidance: Confirm whether informal/shadow accounts need to be migrated into AWS Organizations
Notes: Existing account enrolment adds complexity and risk to Phase 1; requires account preparation steps

Question: What is your preferred approach for the initial workload accounts — pilot with one account first, or provision all environment accounts simultaneously?
Guidance: Piloting reduces risk; simultaneous provisioning accelerates timeline
Notes: Impacts AFT configuration and Phase 3 account vending scope

Question: For the on-premises connectivity cutover (VPN establishment), what is the maximum acceptable disruption to on-premises-to-cloud traffic?
Guidance: If zero downtime is required, dual-connection approach must be designed
Notes: VPN failover configuration and testing plan depends on downtime tolerance

Question: What internal team members are available to support the project and at what capacity? (hours per week per role)
Guidance: List roles: Cloud Engineer, Network Engineer, Security Analyst, FinOps, Application Owner
Notes: Under-resourced customer teams are the #1 cause of landing zone project delays

Question: Who will own the landing zone operationally after handover — an internal team, a managed services provider, or Amatra?
Guidance: Confirm ownership model and whether a managed service or ongoing advisory engagement is desired
Notes: Handover scope and runbook depth depend on the long-term operating model

Question: What training is required for the team taking ownership of the landing zone post-handover?
Guidance: Options: hands-on workshops, recorded sessions, written runbooks, AWS Training courses
Notes: Training scope impacts Phase 3 timeline; complex environments may require 3–5 days of dedicated workshops

Question: What are the acceptance criteria your team will use to sign off on the landing zone at end of Phase 3?
Guidance: Examples: all Control Tower guardrails green, two workload accounts vended via AFT, Security Hub score above threshold
Notes: Formal acceptance criteria prevent scope creep and provide a clear project completion gate

Question: Who has authority to sign off on go-live readiness? (Technical lead, CISO, CTO, Steering Committee)
Guidance: Identify the approver and any committee review process required
Notes: Multi-stakeholder sign-off processes can add 1–2 weeks to Phase 3; plan accordingly

Question: Is there a formal change management or change advisory board (CAB) process that AWS infrastructure changes must pass through?
Guidance: Describe the CAB cadence and lead time required for change approvals
Notes: CAB approval cycles must be factored into phase transition planning and cutover scheduling

Question: What documentation deliverables are required at project close? (Architecture diagrams, runbooks, decision records, as-built documentation)
Guidance: List required documents and any templates that must be used
Notes: Documentation scope impacts Phase 3 effort estimate; confirm format requirements (Confluence, Word, PDF)

Question: Is AWS Direct Connect being considered? If so, has a provider been selected and has the lead time been confirmed?
Guidance: Direct Connect provisioning can take 4–12 weeks depending on location and provider
Notes: If Direct Connect is required by go-live, it must be ordered in Week 1 of the project to avoid timeline slippage

Question: Are there any third-party security or network tools (SIEM, CASB, NGFW) that must be in place before workloads can be onboarded?
Guidance: List tools, vendors, and procurement/deployment status
Notes: Undeployed third-party tooling can block workload onboarding; confirm procurement timelines

Question: Are there any constraints on the Terraform or IaC tooling version? (e.g. enterprise policy mandating specific Terraform version or HashiCorp licencing restrictions)
Guidance: Note the BSL licence change introduced in Terraform 1.6+ and OpenTofu as an alternative
Notes: Licencing constraints may require a pivot to OpenTofu or AWS CDK; must be resolved before AFT pipeline design

Question: Does your organisation have an existing AWS account creation process that Account Factory for Terraform will replace?
Guidance: Describe any existing manual or ticket-based provisioning workflows that need to be decommissioned
Notes: Parallel processes create governance risk; old provisioning methods must be formally retired at Phase 3 go-live

Question: What organisational risks could delay stakeholder availability or decision-making during the 3-month engagement?
Guidance: Examples: upcoming M&A activity, leadership changes, competing IT projects, regulatory audits
Notes: Proactive risk identification allows contingency planning and realistic timeline management
